source.title: Temporal-sequential modeling for remaining useful life estimation of turbofan engine
source.authors: Rajneesh Kumar; Shivam Ojha; A. Shelke; Anowarul Habib

record.file_problem: The text is a full article in press, though the authors note it is an unedited version that may contain errors.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizers and dropout on held-out turbofan RUL prediction, extending those comparisons to a time-series regression setting outside the image-classification and language benchmarks named in V4 and the classifier settings in V6.
record.gate_note: The study does not test random-label memorization, generalization on natural labels, width beyond interpolation, CNN versus fully connected image classifiers, batch size effects, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Its optimizer and dropout comparisons report held-out prediction metrics in a distinct RUL task.
record.test_reason: The study compares optimizers and dropout in CNN–LSTM remaining-useful-life regression. V4 concerns image-classification and language benchmarks, and V6 concerns classifiers. These regression results concern related questions but do not test the supplied versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: SGD achieves the lowest FD001 RMSE, Adam achieves the lowest NASA score, and dropout slightly improves RMSE while worsening NASA score. The authors favor SGD overall and attribute improved generalization to dropout, although the reported metrics show a tradeoff.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a CNN–LSTM for RUL regression on simulated turbofan sensor sequences, comparing optimizers and dropout; the claim versions concern generalization on natural labels and classifier or language-model settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice changes the reported RMSE and NASA score; adding dropout changes RMSE and NASA score in opposite directions. The study also reports window-size variation, but it does not test a claim version.

fits_no_version.finding: On FD001 RUL regression, SGD has the lowest RMSE among five optimizers. Adam has the lowest NASA score: 281.31 versus SGD's 295.16. All optimizers use the same learning-rate schedule and otherwise default optimizer parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer rankings for CNN–LSTM RUL regression depend on the evaluation metric under a shared training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding dropout lowers RMSE slightly, from 12.91 to 12.79, while increasing the NASA score from 275.67 to 295.16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout can have mixed effects on symmetric and asymmetric held-out error measures in CNN–LSTM RUL regression.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison reports test metrics but no corresponding training error, so it does not directly measure the training-to-test gap. Table 5 gives Adadelta RMSE 22.79, while sections 6.1 and 6.4 give 22.57. The dropout comparison is on one dataset and uses both RMSE and NASA score, which move in different directions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width increases beyond the threshold for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons on image-classification or language benchmarks, including tuning, weight decay, switching optimizers, and word-level language modeling.
Batch-size comparisons with fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects in classifiers, including small-data regimes, excessive dropout, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: Section 6.4 and Figure 7 do report training and validation loss trajectories; the record's claim that no training-error comparison is reported is too strong. Numerical final training losses and a controlled comparison at matched training performance are unavailable in the supplied text. Missing training-loss evidence would not itself justify a limits_scope label, since V4 does not require adaptive methods always to have equal or better training performance.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Image-classification and language benchmarks; broad tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Fully connected and convolutional classification, small training sets, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples and comparing with random-example removal.

rows.subject: CNN–LSTM model trained with SGD
rows.operation_detail: Train the same CNN–LSTM architecture with the specified optimizer and evaluate on FD001 test data.
rows.note: Reference optimizer in the optimizer comparison; lowest reported RMSE.
rows.check: The reported RMSE of 12.79 is correct, but this RUL regressor is outside V4's stated benchmark scope. SGD alone is also a reference condition rather than an adaptive-versus-SGD effect.

rows.subject: CNN–LSTM model trained with Adam
rows.operation_detail: Train the same CNN–LSTM architecture with the specified optimizer and evaluate on FD001 test data.
rows.note: Adam's RMSE is higher than SGD's, but the study reports no training-error comparison.
rows.check: Adam's RMSE of 13.63 versus SGD's 12.79 is correct, but the comparison concerns RUL regression rather than V4's image or language benchmarks.

rows.subject: CNN–LSTM model trained with RMSprop
rows.operation_detail: Train the same CNN–LSTM architecture with the specified optimizer and evaluate on FD001 test data.
rows.note: RMSprop's RMSE is higher than SGD's, but the study reports no training-error comparison.
rows.check: RMSprop's RMSE of 14.32 versus SGD's 12.79 is correct, but this regression comparison does not measure V4 in its stated scope.

rows.subject: CNN–LSTM model trained with Adagrad
rows.operation_detail: Train the same CNN–LSTM architecture with the specified optimizer and evaluate on FD001 test data.
rows.note: Adagrad's RMSE is higher than SGD's, but the study reports no training-error comparison.
rows.check: Adagrad's RMSE of 19.17 versus SGD's 12.79 is correct, but this regression comparison does not measure V4 in its stated scope.

rows.subject: CNN–LSTM model trained with Adadelta
rows.operation_detail: Train the same CNN–LSTM architecture with the specified optimizer and evaluate on FD001 test data.
rows.note: Table 5 reports 22.79; section 6.1 and section 6.4 report 22.57 for Adadelta RMSE.
rows.check: This regression comparison is outside V4. Table 5 reports Adadelta RMSE 22.79, whereas sections 6.1 and 6.4 report 22.57; the discrepancy cannot be resolved from the supplied text.

rows.subject: CNN–LSTM (Full Model)
rows.operation_detail: Train the CNN–LSTM with dropout and evaluate on FD001 test data.
rows.note: The authors describe a small RMSE reduction with dropout; the NASA score moves in the opposite direction.
rows.check: The RMSE reduction from 12.91 without dropout to 12.79 with dropout is correctly recorded, but it concerns a regressor rather than the classifiers named in V6.

rows.subject: CNN–LSTM (Full Model)
rows.operation_detail: Train the CNN–LSTM with dropout and evaluate on FD001 test data.
rows.note: Lower NASA score indicates better performance; the score increases with dropout.
rows.check: The NASA score increase from 275.67 to 295.16 is correct and indicates worse asymmetric prediction performance, but this regression metric does not establish a reversal of V6's classifier claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
